name: Battersea Park January Running Festival
course: Flat paved park paths with multiple laps and a track-area finish.
transport: Limited paid park parking; Battersea Power Station, Queenstown Road and Clapham Junction serve the area.
facilities: Bag drop, toilets, chip timing and lap water.
rules: Minimum ages: half 17, 10K 15, 5K 11. Contact organiser if expecting over three hours; no dogs in Millennium Arena.
reason: A late-morning winter start on flat tarmac helps runners test pace; limited parking and separate distance split points favour an early arrival by rail.

name: Tatton Park January 5K & 10K
course: Undulating footpaths and park roads. Park opens to vehicles at 10:00; follow marshals if still running.
transport: Free on-site parking, with marshals from 06:45; Knutsford station about half a mile from park entrance.
facilities: Bag drop, toilets, 10K halfway water; no 5K course water.
rules: Packs collected on day, 10K by 08:15, 5K by 08:35. Keep distance from free-roaming deer and sheep.
reason: Early pack collection and possible vehicle sharing after 10:00 matter more than the scenic setting when planning this winter race.

name: Finsbury Park January Running Festival
course: Tarmac park paths; half nine laps plus mini loop, 10K four plus mini loop, 5K two.
transport: Public transport recommended; no specified event parking. Event village at athletics track.
facilities: Bag drop, portable toilets and water at 5km point.
rules: All packs collected on day; half collection 08:00–09:00. Page contains stale November prose, so confirm final January guide.
reason: The half's nine laps suit frequent spectator support but require careful lap counting. No event parking and on-day pack collection affect arrival.

name: Victoria Park January Running Festival
course: Flat, wide park paths. Half and 5K starts are a walk from the village.
transport: Use Hackney Wick, Mile End, Bow Road or Homerton; nearby parking is limited.
facilities: Bag drop, toilets, course water and village food trucks.
rules: Early entrants receive mailed packs; later entries collect on day. Allow time to reach your separate start line.
reason: A flat pace test with three distances, but the half and 5K do not start at the village. Pack delivery depends on entry date.

name: Battersea Park February Running Festival
course: Flat paved park laps with a track-area finish.
transport: Rail or Tube recommended; in-park paid parking is limited.
facilities: Bag drop, toilets, water every lap and chip timing.
rules: Half pack collection closes 10:00; 5K/10K at 10:45. Contact organiser if expecting over three hours.
reason: The later start is convenient for winter travel, but half-marathon pack collection ends 30 minutes before the gun.

name: Carsington Water Trail February
start: Half 09:30 from visitor centre; 10K 10:00 from Millfields car park.
course: Undulating reservoir trails; flags and arrows supplemented by GPX for self-navigation.
transport: Paid parking at both starts; 10K finish is 1.3 miles from its start, about a 25-minute walk back.
facilities: Bag transport from 10K start, toilets at both sites, 10K water at 5km and half water at miles 3, 6 and 9.
rules: Minimum age half 17, 10K 15; route unsuitable for wheelchairs or prams.
reason: The 10K's separate start and finish make parking choice consequential. Winter trail footing, 200m half ascent and GPX navigation are worth preparing for.

name: Victoria Park February Running Festival
course: Flat park paths; half and 5K starts are separate from the event village.
transport: St Marks Gate hub; Hackney Wick, Mile End, Bow Road and Homerton are nearby. Parking limited.
facilities: Bag drop, portable toilets, water on course, food and coffee in village.
rules: Give yourself extra time to walk to the start. Dogs cannot run; buggy and wheelchair participants welcomed.
reason: A late-winter flat course for pacing, with a useful Saturday date. Separate start points are the main logistics trap.

name: Richmond Park February Half Marathon & 10K
course: Four-lap half on trail paths, pavement and grass, with undulations and deer habitat.
transport: Mortlake station about 20 minutes' walk; Richmond station 30–40 minutes. Village near Sheen Gate.
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village.
rules: No formal cutoff, but contact organiser if expecting over three hours. Check the 10K's separate route information.
reason: The four laps and 187m of half-marathon climbing make it a different effort from flat London parks; rail arrival needs a walking allowance.
